newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: U.N. hits delay in tracing missing in Bosnia.
newsitem.headline: U.N. hits delay in tracing missing in Bosnia.

text.p: The Security Council expressed concern on Thursday at the lack of progress in establishing the fate of thousands of missing persons in Bosnia by exhuming bodies and other means and mainly blamed obstruction by the Bosnian Serb authorities.
"It notes with concern that the fate of only a few hundred missing persons have been so far established," a statement read by council President Gerardo Martinez Blanco of Honduras said.

"The Security Council is concerned that endeavours by the relevant international authorities to identify the fate of the missing by inter alia carrying out exhumations has met with limited success largely due to obstruction by Republika Srpska," the statement said, referring to the Bosnian Serb entity.

An official of the International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC) was quoted on Wednesday as saying some 14,000 Bosnians, including Moslems, Serbs and Croats, who went missing during the war were still unaccounted for a year after the fighting ended.
"We are still searching for 14,000 people," Raoul Bittel, the ICRC chief in central Bosnia, told the state news agency HINA after talks with local officials in the central town of Novi Travnik.
He said there were indications that a majority of the missing were dead. "In this time of peace our main duty is to search for the missing," he said.

The Security Council statement welcomed a recent visit by a Republika Srpska delgation to the U.N. Yugoslav war crimes tribunal at The Hague and hoped this would facilitate future cooperation in investigations by tribunal personnel.
"The Security Council condemns all attempts to obstruct the investigations or to destroy, alter, conceal or damage any related evidence," it said.

The council stressed the obligation of all parties to cooperate fully and unconditionally with such investigations and reiterated that violations of international humanitarian law throughout Bosnia and Herzegovina must be fully investigated.
